title: El periódico
goal: Buy a paper and get told the news before you read it
culture: The man at the kiosk reads every paper he sells and will tell you what is in it whether you ask or not. That summary is the better half of what you are buying, and asking for it out loud is what turns a sale into a conversation.

beats.good: Periódico, and on this corner it means La Prensa unless you say otherwise.

beats.objective: Ask what the news is today
beats.en: And what does it say today?
beats.good: ¿Qué dice? asks the paper and the man at once, and he will answer for both. It is the cheapest conversation in Granada.

beats.es: Uh. Lo de siempre, pues: que suben los precios, que no hay luz en Xalteva.
beats.objective: Agree that the news is never good
beats.good: Ni modo after bad news is agreement, not despair. It is how a complaint gets put down here.
Lo de siempre makes you a regular in three words, and it works the same at the comedor and the pulpería.
